text:
kevin: Brain dump: proposing a "conductive-grid" pattern to shrink the hotpath coupling. idea: small ephemeral local caches colocated with executors + a lightweight global control plane that distributes affinity assignments. intent is to make prefix churn local and let executors remain stateless for easier rollbacks.

tara: can you TL;DR the migration steps?

kevin: Stage 0: feature-flag router to emit affinity headers but no change in path. Stage 1: deploy grid control plane (read-only) and attach ephemeral caches to executors in observe mode. Stage 2: enable read-through for a limited tenant cohort. Stage 3: flip writes + expand.

jordi: latency worry: extra steering RPCs. how do we keep tail low?

kevin: keep steering async where possible. router adds an affinity hint header; executor consults local ephemeral cache first (O(1)). grid control plane only consulted on miss or reassign. goal: median delta <0.5ms, p95 delta budget 10-15%.

sylvie: warming strategy? filling ephemeral caches for large tenants could be slow.

kevin: three-pronged: 1) backfill top-k prefixes per tenant with a bounded snapshot job, 2) shadow traffic to populate caches, 3) lazy population on miss with write-behind to grid store. track warmup curves.

tara: tenant-owned heuristics live in enrichment. do we move them?

jordi: suggest a compatibility shim: allow the grid to proxy selective enrichment calls during transition. longer term, migrate heuristics to enrichment adapters and remove shim.

kevin: safety gates: very small canaries during high QPS (0.1%), larger outside peak (3%), with 48h observation windows. automated rollback triggers: p95 > baseline+20%, error rate increase >0.05% absolute, or output-diff >0.25% on eval set for classifiers.

sylvie: test harness: replay 50k sessions with injected network jitter and node failures. include hallucination-sensitive prompts. thresholds: label drift <0.2%, BLEU-like gen delta <1.0.

kevin: config example for router weights + fallback we can plumb into console:
```
steer:
  policy: grid_hint
  timeout_ms: 80
  fallback: legacy-exec
  cache_ttl_ms: 150
```

tara: observability checklist: per-tenant cache-hit, grid-miss rate, prefix-populate-rate, executor-batch-size, token-latency histograms, output diff alarms. tag traces with `grid_phase` and `cache_status`.

jordi: prometheus snippets to watch: `sum(rate(grid_rpc_total[1m])) by (code)` and `histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(token_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le, grid_phase))`. Also `sum(rate(ephemeral_cache_hits[5m])) by (tenant)`.

kevin: migration job plan: snapshot top-200k prefixes per tenant into an S3 bucket, stream into grid store with backpressure, run nightly reconciliation for 7 days while shadowing 100% traffic for monitoring only. only enable writes after mismatch rate <0.05%.

sylvie: cost: extra egress + grid CPU. roll out to small tenants first and model cost-per-1k-reqs. include per-tenant cost delta in rollout doc.

kevin: fallback semantics: executor consults local cache; on miss it queries grid with `timeout_ms=80`; if grid fails or times out, executor falls back to legacy path and flags a miss metric so we can monitor.

jordi: minor nit: define sequence semantics for prefix updates. we should use monotonic version numbers per prefix and idempotent apply in grid store.

kevin: agreed. add a reconciliation job that detects out-of-order or missing seqs and attempts repair.

tara: who owns the shim and reconciliation? kevin will own grid control plane, jordi will own reconciliation, sylvie will own rollout ops.

deploy-bot: infra note: feature-flag `conductive_grid_observe` created. CI: https://ci.redwood.example/builds/31021 (artifacts staged).

sylvie: I'll draft an RFC follow-up with timeline: 2w spike, 3w infra prep, 2w pilot, 6-10w phased expansion. will include canary playbook, dashboard mocks, and cost estimates. tagging reviewers: @kevin @jordi @tara. :white_check_mark:
